title: Tariq Barma pitches Perimeter Solutions at Sohn 2026
description: Tariq Barma, Co-Founder and Managing Partner, Balance Capital Partners, argues that Perimeter Solutions is a "misunderstood winner" poised for significant growth as part of "Next Wave" at the Sohn Investment Conference 2026.
summary: The pitch argues that Perimeter Solutions is a misunderstood winner with normalized earnings power that is currently materially underappreciated. The presenter expects the stock to double over the next 2 to 3 years, driven primarily by earnings growth and the deployment of capital into high-return M&A, which will evolve the company from a cyclical fire business into a collection of niche advantage businesses. While the presenter acknowledges skepticism regarding management and the incentive compensation structure, they believe the company has already hit 'escape velocity' and that management's history of opportunistic buybacks supports their ability to create value. A key catalyst is the expectation that the Retardant business will grow to represent 30% of EBITDA by 2030.

claims.claim: The presenter argues Perimeter Solutions is a misunderstood winner with normalized earnings power materially underappreciated, expecting a base case double over 2-3 years driven by earnings growth and M&A.
claims.quote: Our thesis is that normalized earnings power is still materially under appreciated. We expect the company will grow pro forma EBITDA north of 30% in the coming years while handily beating estimates and seeing positive revisions.
claims.speaker: Tariq Barma

claims.claim: The presenter expects a base case double over the next 2 to 3 years, with most return coming from earnings growth and potential multiple expansion in a bull case.
claims.quote: This will result in a base case double over the next 2 to 3 years. Most of the return comes from earnings growth. In a bull case, multiple expansion will drive further upside.
claims.speaker: Tariq Barma

claims.claim: The presenter identifies downside risk of about 20% in a scenario where market perception shifts to view the company as a declining commodity chemical supplier.
claims.quote: And in a scenario where market perception dramatically shifts and the company is viewed as a declining commodity chemical supplier. We think there's about 20% downside.
claims.speaker: Tariq Barma

claims.claim: The presenter believes Perimeter has already hit escape velocity and will deploy significant capital into high-return M&A, evolving from a cyclical fire company to a collection of niche advantage businesses.
claims.quote: Perimeter has already hit escape velocity. And the next chapter will come from the company executing on a value-creating M&A. We expect them to deploy significant amounts of capital at attractive returns.
claims.speaker: Tariq Barma

claims.claim: The presenter notes management opportunistically repurchased 16% of the company over the last 5 years at attractive prices, supporting the idea they can create value on acquired businesses.
claims.quote: Management opportunistically repurchased 16% of the company over the last 5 years at attractive prices. They've improved every business line they've operated, which supports the idea that they can do the same on acquired businesses to create value.
claims.speaker: Tariq Barma

claims.claim: The presenter states that by 2030, they think the Retardant business will be 30% of EBITDA as the company evolves and deploys capital into high-return M&A.
claims.quote: By 2030, we think Retardant will be 30% of EBITDA. The market sees a cyclical fire company with no clear comp set, so it gets lumped in with chemicals or oil services.
claims.speaker: Tariq Barma

claims.claim: The presenter concludes that Perimeter is a misunderstood winner and they like the stock, despite skepticism about management and the incentive comp structure.
claims.quote: In conclusion, we think Perimeter is a misunderstood winner. We like the stock. Thank you.
claims.speaker: Tariq Barma
